comments.title: Electrical Plan Missing Infrastructure Completeness Certification Note
comments.comment: No note appears on the Electrical Design Plan certifying that all existing and proposed electric infrastructure is shown or identifying exceptions that require Austin Energy pre-approval.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires plans to include an affirmative note confirming that all electric infrastructure (existing and proposed) is depicted, with exceptions identified as requiring Austin Energy pre-approval. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and related utility sheets contain no such statement. The closest language — Sheet 3 note #5 stating 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date' — implies incompleteness rather than confirming completeness. Without this note, Austin Energy cannot verify the design is complete or identify intentional omissions subject to later approval.
comments.sheets: Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); General Notes (Sheet 3); Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19)
comments.applicableArea: All utility plans; Electrical Design Plan — note requirement
comments.resolution: Add the following note to Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan): 'All existing and proposed electric infrastructure required for service to this project is shown on this plan. Any modifications, additional facilities, or deviations from the shown design require pre-approval from Austin Energy Design. Exceptions or items not yet designed are noted separately or subject to Austin Energy Design approval.'

perRunFindings.comment: No note confirming that all electric infrastructure (existing and proposed) is documented on plans or specifying that exceptions require Austin Energy pre-approval. Add explicit note stating: 'All existing and proposed electric infrastructure is shown on these plans. Any exceptions or deviations from shown facilities require Austin Energy pre-approval.'
perRunFindings.observation: Sheets 3, 9, 19, and 21 show various electric infrastructure elements (existing and proposed) and contain notes addressing utility requirements and construction procedures. However, no explicit note statement appears on any sheet confirming that 'all electric infrastructure is shown including new and existing' or stating that 'exceptions require Austin Energy pre-approval.' The closest language is Sheet 3 note #5 stating 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date,' which implies incompleteness rather than confirming completeness.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) is the foundational requirement for Land Development Review applications. A definitive statement that all electric infrastructure (existing and proposed) is shown is critical for applicant certification and Austin Energy review. The absence of this confirmation statement leaves ambiguity about whether the plans represent complete documentation or partial submittal pending AE approval. This statement is required as formal certification.

perRunFindings.comment: Note missing stating all electric infrastructure (existing and proposed) is shown and exceptions require Austin Energy pre-approval. Please add: 'All existing and proposed electric infrastructure is shown on these plans. Any modifications to electric service, additional facilities, or changes to the shown design require pre-approval from Austin Energy Design. Indicate any infrastructure not yet designed or to be determined.'
applicableAreas: Utility plan, electrical design plan, site plan
perRunFindings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) for a note stating that all electric infrastructure is shown. Sheet 21 contains 'Utility Notes' (Block 6 from guide.md) with contractor directives to verify utilities but no note stating 'All electric infrastructure including existing and proposed is shown on these plans, or exceptions requiring pre-approval are noted.' The plan shows existing OHE, proposed transformers, and proposed routing but does not include a comprehensive statement that the electric design is complete.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) is the comprehensive requirements section for plan documentation. A standard practice and requirement is for plans to include a note certifying that all existing and proposed electric infrastructure is shown, and if anything is omitted or to be designed later (exceptions), those items must be noted with the requirement for AE pre-approval. This note provides AE Design certainty that the applicant has identified all infrastructure and indicates any gaps. Its absence means AE Design cannot verify the design is complete.

perRunFindings.comment: Note missing stating all electric infrastructure shown and exceptions require AE pre-approval. Add a note to the electrical design plan stating: 'All existing and proposed electric infrastructure required for service to this project is shown on this plan, except where noted separately or subject to Austin Energy Design approval.'
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) is reviewed for the presence of a note stating that all electric infrastructure (existing and proposed) is shown on the plan or noting exceptions requiring AE pre-approval. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 explicitly confirms: 'No, there is no note at the top or anywhere else on the sheet with that specific phrasing or similar language indicating completeness of the electric infrastructure shown.' The sheet contains general utility notes (Block 6 on the blocks.md states 'Contractor shall verify horizontal and vertical location of existing utilities' and disclaimers about existing utility locations). However, there is no affirmative statement indicating that all existing and proposed electric infrastructure requiring approval has been shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan, nor any notation of exceptions that require separate AE approval.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires that plans show 'All existing electric facilities (transmission/distribution structures, guys, anchors, transformers)' and 'All existing and proposed permanent structures' and 'Sufficient clearances demonstrated for existing and proposed electric facilities.' Without a note stating that all infrastructure is shown (or exceptions noted), reviewers cannot determine whether missing elements are intentional omissions subject to later AE approval or unintentional oversights. The Regulatory Overview section lists common violation patterns: 'Missing plat note requirements' and identifies that the grouping addresses 'what must be shown on plans to demonstrate a complete electric design.' A note confirming completeness or documenting exceptions is essential to that completeness demonstration. The title 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' suggests the design is not yet final, but even preliminary submissions must include a note about completeness or noted exceptions.

comments.title: Electric Facilities Absent or Inconsistent Across Required Plan Sheets
comments.comment: Proposed electric facilities shown in detail on Sheet 21 are missing from, or inconsistently depicted on, the Site Plan, Landscape Plan, Grading Plan, and Utility Tap Plan, with mismatched equipment symbols and facility locations across sheets.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires electric facilities to be shown consistently across all applicable plan sheets so design disciplines can coordinate. The following deficiencies exist:
- **Sheet 9 (Site Plan):** Shows only one 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' on the western side; individual meters, pull boxes, and underground conduit routing to specific buildings are not depicted
- **Sheet 11 (Grading Plan):** Shows electric easements only; no electric lines, equipment, conduit routing, or transformer pads are shown
- **Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan):** Legend symbol for 'Proposed Underground Electric' exists but no actual electric facilities are drawn on the plan
- **Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan):** Existing overhead electric on boundary shown; no transformer pads, meters, pull boxes, or underground routing depicted — preventing verification of tree clearances and landscaping coordination in staging areas
- **Equipment symbol inconsistency:** Sheet 21 uses large colored rectangles with zig-zag symbols for transformers and small circles with 'E' for pull boxes; Sheet 9 uses text label 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)'; Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) uses a square 'T' symbol — no consistent legend across sheets
- **Facility location mismatch:** Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads at specific locations (NW, SW, central-south, central-east); Sheet 9 shows only one transformer whose location does not clearly correspond to any of the four pads on Sheet 21; Sheet 31 shows no transformer pads at all
comments.sheets: Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); Site Plan (Sheet 9); Grading Plan (Sheet 11); Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19); Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
comments.applicableArea: All sheets showing electric equipment; transformer pad locations (NW, SW, central-south, central-east); meter locations; pull box locations; underground conduit routing
comments.resolution: Update Sheets 9, 11, 19, and 31 to show all proposed electric facilities — all 4 transformer pads, meters, pull boxes, and underground conduit routing — at locations consistent with Sheet 21. Establish a single equipment legend defining symbols for transformer pads, meters, pull boxes, and disconnects, and apply identical symbols and labels on every sheet depicting electric facilities; include this legend on each such sheet. Verify that each facility's mapped location is consistent across all sheets using common coordinate or dimension references.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Symbol inconsistency (EL-10.34) and location mismatch (EL-10.35) sub-items were each flagged by only 1/3 runs; the core finding of missing electric facilities on required sheets (EL-10.33) was flagged by 3/3 runs.

perRunFindings.comment: Electric infrastructure (transformers, meters, conduit, easements) verified on Sheets 2, 9, 19, and 21. Full coordination with landscape, grading, irrigation, storm drain, wet utility, and architectural elevation sheets cannot be verified without examining Sheets 10-20, 30-39. Confirm that electric facilities and easements are shown on all applicable plan sheets per UCM § 1.16.0(1).
applicableAreas: Site plan, utility plan, landscape plan, grading plan, irrigation plan, storm drain plan, wet utility plan, architectural elevations (where overhead facilities affect building design)
perRunFindings.observation: Examined Sheets 2 (Plat), 3 (General Notes), 9 (Site Plan), 19 (Utility Tap Plan), and 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan). Electric easements shown on Sheets 2, 9, and 21 with consistent labeling; Sheet 19 legend includes 'E | Proposed Underground Electric' but shows minimal detail. Electric infrastructure (transformers, pull boxes, meters, conduit, overhead lines) explicitly detailed on Sheet 21 and referenced on Sheet 9. However, the site plan package includes 39 sheets total. Did not examine Sheets 4-8 (Survey, Erosion Control), 10-18 (Fire, Grading, Drainage, Storm, Water), 20 (more utilities), 22-29 (Details, Addressing), 30-39 (Landscape, Trees, Wall). Cannot verify whether electric facilities are shown or appropriately coordinated on these remaining sheets.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires that electric facilities be shown on 'all required plan sheets' including landscape (for tree clearances), grading (for equipment location coordination), irrigation (for conflicts with underground facilities), storm drain (for utility coordination), and architectural elevations (for overhead facility clearances to buildings). Without examining landscape, grading, irrigation, storm, and elevation sheets, cannot confirm whether electric infrastructure is consistently shown across the full plan set and properly coordinated to prevent conflicts.

perRunFindings.comment: Electric facilities are not shown on all required plan sheets. The detailed design on Sheet 21 (transformers, meters, routing) must be repeated on: (1) Sheet 9 (Site Plan); (2) Sheet 11 (Grading Plan); (3) Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan); (4) Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan); (5) all other applicable utility, irrigation, and storm drain sheets. Ensure consistency in facility locations and equipment symbols across all sheets.
applicableAreas: Site plan, utility plan, landscape plan, grading plan, storm drain plan, wet utility plan
perRunFindings.observation: Examined all required plan sheets for electric facility depiction. Sheet 21 shows: existing OHE, existing underground lines, 4 proposed transformer pads, 7 meter locations, pull boxes, underground routing. Sheet 9 shows: existing OHE, one transformer pad, electric easements. Sheet 11 shows: electric easements only, NO electric lines or equipment. Sheet 19 shows: legend symbols for electric but NO actual electric facilities drawn on the plan. Sheet 31 shows: existing OHE on boundary, NO transformers, NO meters, NO underground routing, NO pull boxes. Vision analysis confirmed sheets 11 and 19 lack the complete electric design, and sheet 31 is missing transformers and staging areas shown on Sheet 21.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires comprehensive depiction of electric facilities across all plan sheets so all design disciplines can coordinate. Fragmented depiction creates risk of conflicts (e.g., landscaping in transformer staging areas, grading encroaching on underground routing, irrigation lines crossing conduit).

perRunFindings.comment: Electric facilities not shown consistently across all required plan sheets. Show all proposed electric facilities (transformers, pull boxes, meters, underground conduit routing, easements) on Site Plan (Sheet 9), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), and Grading Plan (Sheet 11) with consistent symbols and locations matching Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan).
applicableAreas: Site Plan (Sheet 9), Utility Plan (Sheet 21), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) vision analysis confirms: 'Transformer Pad (Typ.) is explicitly shown and labeled on the west side... Individual meters, pull boxes, and detailed underground electrical conduits routing to the specific buildings are not visibly drawn or labeled on this sheet.' Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows comprehensive electrical facilities (transformers, pull boxes, meters, underground lines) with explicit labels. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) vision analysis states: 'There are no clear labels or specific symbols explicitly identifying electrical facilities such as transformers, meters, or pull boxes on this landscape plan sheet.' Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) guide mentions 'utility easements' but vision analysis reveals electrical infrastructure details are not shown there.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires plans to show electric infrastructure, and the grouping's common violation patterns specifically identify: 'Cross-sheet inconsistency: Electric facilities shown on utility plan but omitted from landscape, grading, or irrigation plans where coordination is critical (especially down guy anchors conflicting with accessible paths, trees conflicting with clearance envelopes).' The principle is that all infrastructure must be consistently shown on all sheets where coordination is necessary.

perRunFindings.comment: Equipment symbols are inconsistent across plan sheets. Please establish a consistent legend for all electrical equipment (transformer pads, meters, pull boxes, disconnects) and apply identical symbols and labels on all plan sheets. Include the legend on each sheet showing electric facilities.
perRunFindings.observation: Examined equipment symbols across sheets. Sheet 21 uses: large blue rectangles with zig-zag symbols for transformers labeled 'Electrical Transformer Pad'; small blue circles with 'E' for pull boxes labeled 'Electrical Pull Box'; rectangles on building walls for meters labeled 'Electrical Meters.' Sheet 9 shows one 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' but the symbol and style may differ. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey legend) defines 'TRANSFORMER ON PAD' with a square 'T' symbol. The symbols are not consistent across sheets in terms of graphical representation and labeling style.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires 'Equipment symbols consistent across plan sheets.' This is essential for plan reviewers and contractors to identify equipment reliably across all sheets. Inconsistent symbols create confusion and increase risk of misidentification (e.g., meter vs. disconnect, transformer vs. telecom box). All equipment of the same type must use identical symbols and labels across all sheets.

perRunFindings.comment: Electric facility locations do not consistently match across plan sheets. Please verify and ensure: (1) all transformer pads shown on Sheet 21 are also shown on Sheets 9, 11, 19, 31 at identical locations; (2) all meters shown on Sheet 21 are also shown on Sheets 9, 31 (landscape elevation); (3) pull boxes and conduit routing shown on Sheet 21 are shown on Sheets 9, 11, 19; (4) use consistent coordinate/dimension references to verify locations match across sheets.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations, meter locations, pull box locations
perRunFindings.observation: Compared facility locations across sheets. Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads at specific locations (NW, SW, central-south, central-east). Sheet 9 shows one transformer labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' on the western side, which may correspond to one of the four on Sheet 21 but location does not clearly match. Sheet 31 (Landscape) shows OHE but NO transformer pads, meaning the transformers shown in detail on Sheet 21 are not depicted on the landscape plan. This prevents landscaping coordination with transformer locations.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires 'Electric facility locations do not match across plan sheets' to be avoided. When the same facility (e.g., a transformer pad) is shown on multiple sheets, it must be in the same location relative to buildings, property lines, and other features. Discrepancies or omissions across sheets create confusion about the actual design and prevent verification of proper coordination (e.g., are trees within transformer access zones? is landscaping in staging areas?).

comments.title: CAD Submission to AE Transmission Engineering Unconfirmed; Plan/Profile Views Missing
comments.comment: Submission of AutoCAD drawings to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering for transmission line review has not been confirmed, the AutoCAD file version cannot be verified, and the Electrical Design Plan does not include plan and profile views depicting transmission line clearances.
comments.issue:
UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires AutoCAD drawings (version 2016 or newer) be submitted to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering when a project involves transmission facilities (≥60kV). Sheet 3 Block 20 confirms a transmission line crosses the property with detailed easement requirements (16 notes, including 25-foot clearance from structures, pre-construction safety meeting requirement, no-dig/no-grade restriction within easement, and 46,000 lb tandem axle road loading for easement access). Three deficiencies exist:
- **CAD submission not confirmed:** No transmittal email, receipt, or documentation confirms that CAD files were delivered to AE Transmission Engineering
- **AutoCAD version unverifiable:** Site plan drawings were reviewed as PDFs; AutoCAD file version (2016 or newer) of submitted files cannot be confirmed from available documentation
- **Missing plan and profile views:** Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) does not include plan and profile views depicting the transmission line in relation to proposed buildings, utilities, drainage, and other infrastructure with clearances labeled per NESC standards
comments.sheets: Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21); General Notes / Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3)
comments.applicableArea: Transmission line easement areas; electrical infrastructure near transmission facilities
comments.resolution: Submit AutoCAD drawings (version 2016 or newer) to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering for transmission line review. Drawings must include: (1) plan view showing the transmission line, all proposed buildings, utilities, drainage, and other infrastructure with labeled separation distances; (2) profile view showing vertical clearances from transmission line conductors to proposed structures and improvements per NESC standards. Provide a transmittal email or receipt confirming delivery to AE Transmission Engineering (contact: Andrew Perez, 512-505-7153 per Sheet 3 Block 20) and documentation showing the AutoCAD file version.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Requires coordination with Austin Energy Transmission Engineering (contact: Andrew Perez, 512-505-7153 per Sheet 3 Block 20) for specialized transmission line review separate from distribution design review.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: CAD submission cannot be confirmed from available PDF documents; reviewer should verify whether CAD files were submitted to AE Transmission Engineering outside the visible submittal package before requiring resubmittal.

perRunFindings.comment: CAD files for Austin Energy Transmission Engineering review not verified as submitted. Provide evidence that AutoCAD files (version 2016 or newer) have been submitted to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering for review of infrastructure near transmission facilities.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 3 Block 20 documents 16 notes about electric transmission lines and easements, confirming that transmission facilities (≥60kV) are present on or near the property. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows electrical infrastructure routing. However, no evidence of CAD files submitted specifically to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering for review was located in the supplementary documents or correspondence. The site plan shows transmission easement requirements but does not document that AutoCAD files were provided to AE Transmission Engineering.
perRunFindings.reasoning: When a project involves or is near AE transmission lines (≥60kV facilities), CAD files must be submitted to AE Transmission Engineering for specialized review per UCM § 1.16.0(1). The presence of transmission easement notes on Sheet 3 confirms that transmission facilities are relevant to this project. The lack of documented submission of CAD files to AE Transmission Engineering represents a gap. AutoCAD drawings must be submitted in version 2016 or newer and include all relevant infrastructure crossing or near transmission lines.

perRunFindings.comment: CAD files submission to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering not confirmed. While transmission line involvement is documented on Sheet 3 with specific engineering requirements, no confirmation that CAD files have been submitted to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering for specialized transmission review is present in supplementary documents. Submit transmittal email or receipt confirming CAD files were provided to AE Transmission Engineering group for transmission crossing analysis.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 3, Block 20 contains detailed Electric Transmission Notes confirming transmission line crosses property with specific requirements (25-foot clearance from structures, pre-construction safety meeting, no digging/grading, 46,000 lb tandem axle road loading for easement access). Andrew Perez contact provided for transmission coordination (512-505-7153). This confirms transmission line involvement. However, whether CAD files have been submitted separately to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering for specialized review is not confirmed in the submitted documentation.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires CAD files be submitted for AE Transmission Engineering review when project involves transmission lines (≥60kV). Sheet 3 Block 20 confirms transmission line is present and requires engineering review. While preliminary design exists on Sheet 21, whether the formal CAD submission package has been delivered to Austin Energy's Transmission Engineering department specifically is not documented in the available pre-processed materials.

perRunFindings.comment: AutoCAD drawings not verified as submitted in version 2016 or newer. Provide AutoCAD drawing files (version 2016 or newer) to Austin Energy in electronic format for transmission engineering review, or provide documentation confirming the AutoCAD version of files already submitted.
perRunFindings.observation: The site plan includes a Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) showing electrical infrastructure. However, no documentation confirms the AutoCAD version of the files (if any CAD files were provided). The site plan sheets themselves appear to be in a PDF or image format, and no specific AutoCAD file version metadata or submission documentation was located indicating that AutoCAD drawings in version 2016 or newer were submitted to Austin Energy.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires that AutoCAD drawings submitted to Austin Energy be in version 2016 or newer format. This is a technical specification for electronic submissions. Without evidence of the AutoCAD file version being submitted or documentation of file version metadata, it cannot be verified that this requirement has been met.

perRunFindings.comment: AutoCAD file version not verifiable. While site plan drawings are provided, the version of AutoCAD files submitted to Austin Energy cannot be confirmed from available documentation. Verify and document that all CAD files submitted to Austin Energy (Design and Transmission Engineering) are AutoCAD 2016 or newer format. Provide submission confirmation or file properties documentation showing version.
perRunFindings.observation: Site plan sheets are provided as processed documents. No metadata regarding AutoCAD file version (2016 or newer) is available from the pre-processed documentation. Sheet 21 and other sheets show professional design layout but version information of the source CAD files is not accessible.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires AutoCAD files submitted for transmission or land development review be version 2016 or newer. Since transmission line involvement is confirmed (Sheet 3 Block 20), AutoCAD submissions are required. However, the version of CAD files used cannot be verified from the available documentation. This is an accessibility issue with the pre-processed materials rather than a definitive pass/fail determination.

perRunFindings.comment: AutoCAD drawings not verified as submitted to Austin Energy reviewer for transmission line review. Submit all electrical and site design drawings in AutoCAD format (version 2016 or newer) to Austin Energy Transmission Engineering for review of infrastructure near transmission facilities.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 3 Block 20 documents extensive transmission line easement requirements (16 notes), confirming that transmission facilities (≥60kV) are on the property. However, no documentation confirms that AutoCAD drawings showing the electrical design and site infrastructure have been submitted to the Austin Energy reviewer for transmission line review. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan exists but submission of the AutoCAD version to AE reviewers is not verified.
perRunFindings.reasoning: When a project involves transmission lines (≥60kV facilities) or development is within 100 feet of transmission line wires, AutoCAD drawings must be submitted to the Austin Energy reviewer for transmission line review per UCM § 1.16.0(1). The presence of transmission easement notes confirms transmission facilities are relevant. The absence of documented submission of AutoCAD drawings to AE Transmission Engineering represents a deficiency in the submission requirements.

perRunFindings.comment: AutoCAD drawings showing transmission line plan and profile views not provided. Transmission engineering analysis requires plan and profile drawings depicting the transmission line and proposed site infrastructure (buildings, drainage, utilities) with clearances and separation demonstrated in plan and elevation. Prepare and submit detailed plan and profile drawings showing transmission line, proposed buildings, and all infrastructure in AutoCAD format, with clearances labeled per National Electric Safety Code (NESC) standards.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 3, Block 20 confirms transmission line crosses property and provides detailed transmission requirements. However, Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) does NOT show plan and profile views of the transmission line relationship to proposed infrastructure. The transmission line is mentioned in notes on Sheet 3 but is not graphically depicted with clearances and spatial relationships in detail on electrical drawings. No separate transmission design drawing submitted.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires AutoCAD drawings be submitted to Austin Energy transmission reviewer 'when project involves transmission lines' and specifically requires 'plan and profile views' showing how proposed infrastructure relates to transmission facilities. While Sheet 3 documents transmission presence and requirements, the electrical design drawings (Sheet 21) do not show transmission line with plan/profile views demonstrating safe clearances and separation.

comments.title: Separate Austin Energy Distribution Plan with Profile Views Not Submitted
comments.comment: A standalone Austin Energy Distribution Plan with plan and profile views showing detailed electrical service design has not been submitted; the electrical design is shown only on Sheet 21 integrated into the site plan package.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires a separate Austin Energy Distribution Plan with detailed electrical design and plan/profile views when modifications to existing AE facilities are proposed. The project proposes underground service extensions to 8 buildings with 4 transformer pads and associated pull boxes and meters, which constitutes AE facility modifications. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) is integrated into the 39-sheet site plan set and does not include profile views or specifications for cable depths, duct bank configurations, cable sizes/types, service feed details per building, or clearances from other utilities. No standalone AE Distribution Plan document was located in the submittal package.
comments.applicableArea: Electric facility modifications; entire site electric service infrastructure
comments.resolution: Prepare and submit a separate Austin Energy Distribution Plan document (not integrated within the site plan sheet set) showing: plan and profile views of all underground cable routing with depths; duct bank and conduit specifications; transformer pad details; service feeds to each of the 8 buildings; cable sizes and types; and clearances from other utilities — all per Austin Energy standards.
comments.crossDepartmentNote: Typically requires coordination with Austin Energy Design (reviewer: Rosemary Avila per Master Comment Report) to prepare or approve the Distribution Plan as a standalone AE document.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Run-1 was unclear — confirm whether modifications to existing AE distribution facilities are proposed, as this determines whether a separate AE Distribution Plan is required; run-2 treats it as a clear fail.

perRunFindings.comment: Austin Energy Distribution Plan not verified as submitted. If modifications to existing Austin Energy facilities are proposed, provide a separate Austin Energy Distribution Plan showing detailed electrical design with plan and profile views.
perRunFindings.observation: The site plan includes a Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) showing proposed electrical infrastructure layout. However, no separate Austin Energy Distribution Plan with detailed electrical design showing plan and profile views was located in the supplementary documents or as part of the submitted site plan sheets. The preliminary design is shown on the site plan itself, but a separate, dedicated AE Distribution Plan document is not evidenced in the submission.
perRunFindings.reasoning: When modifications to existing AE facilities are proposed, a separate Austin Energy Distribution Plan showing detailed electrical design with plan and profile views is required per UCM § 1.16.0(1). This is a formal document prepared by or in coordination with AE Design. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan on Sheet 21 shows the applicant's proposed routing and equipment, but this may not meet the requirement for a formal AE Distribution Plan if modifications to existing AE facilities are involved. Without documentation of existing AE facility modifications required, the necessity of this item depends on the scope of work affecting existing AE infrastructure.

perRunFindings.comment: Austin Energy Distribution Plan showing detailed design not submitted separately from site plan. Submit detailed Austin Energy Distribution Plan as a separate document showing plan and profile views of all electric service infrastructure, including proposed underground cable routing with depths, duct specifications, transformer pad details, service feeds to each building, clearances from other utilities, and cable size/type specifications per Austin Energy standards.
perRunFindings.observation: Sheet 21 shows preliminary electrical design with proposed transformer pads, pull boxes, and underground routing. However, no separate Austin Energy Distribution Plan is submitted showing detailed electrical design with plan and profile views independent from the site plan. The electrical design is shown on Sheet 21 integrated with the general site plan, not as a standalone AE distribution plan document. No callouts reference an AE Distribution Plan for detailed design with underground routing specifications, cable depths, or clearance details.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires 'Austin Energy Distribution Plan not submitted separate from site plan showing detailed electrical design with plan and profile views when modifications to existing AE facilities are proposed.' The transmission easement and service extension to 8 buildings constitute AE facility modifications requiring detailed design. The preliminary status of Sheet 21 and integration with site plan (rather than as a standalone AE distribution design document) indicates this requirement may not be satisfied. A separate, detailed distribution plan with profile views showing cable depths, duct banks, transformer specifications, and service feeds is needed.

comments.title: Title Commitment or Easement Encumbrance Report Not Submitted to Austin Energy
comments.comment: No title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey certified to show all existing easement encumbrances has been confirmed as submitted to Austin Energy for review of proposed electric easements.
comments.issue: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires that for all sites with proposed or modified electric easements, applicants submit to Austin Energy a title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey showing all easement encumbrances. The project has six documented existing easements of record (greenbelt access, drainage, wastewater, public utility, and additional drainage easements) and proposes new electric easements. No title document was located in the submittal package, the Project Review Form does not reference title document submission to Austin Energy, and the Engineer's Summary Letter does not document such submission. Austin Energy coordination is active via Bluebeam (reviewer: Rosemary Avila per Master Comment Report), but the specific documents submitted through that portal cannot be verified from available materials.
comments.applicableArea: All proposed and modified electric easement areas
comments.resolution: Obtain and submit to Austin Energy a title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey certified to show all existing easements and encumbrances affecting the property. Provide documentation (e.g., transmittal record) confirming delivery to Austin Energy reviewer Rosemary Avila.
comments.reviewerAttentionNote: Low confidence (1/3 runs fail, 1/3 runs unclear); reviewer should verify whether title documents were submitted through the Austin Energy Bluebeam coordination portal (referenced in Master Comment Report) before requiring resubmittal.

perRunFindings.comment: No title commitment, ALTA survey, or Ownership and Encumbrance Report visible in submitted documents; Austin Energy coordination active via Bluebeam but document submission cannot be verified from available materials
applicableAreas: All proposed or modified electric easements; coordination with Austin Energy
perRunFindings.observation: No title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey is visible in the submitted site plan documents or supplementary document overviews examined. The Master Comment Report (Electric Review section) identifies Austin Energy (Rosemary Avila, rosemary.avila@austinenergy.com) as the reviewer and references a Bluebeam link (https://studio.bluebeam.com/share/epcafnizivuefw) where Austin Energy has posted site-specific comments for the applicant's response in blue. This indicates that Austin Energy coordination is active and that the applicant HAS submitted materials for Austin Energy review. However, the specific content of what documents were submitted (title documents, easement reports) cannot be verified from the visible site plan sheets or supplementary documents provided for this review. The Bluebeam link is not accessible to this reviewer.
perRunFindings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires that for all sites with proposed or modified electric easements, applicants must submit to Austin Energy a title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey 'showing all easement encumbrances' for Austin Energy review to verify adequacy of existing easements and identify conflicts. The grouping guidance states to 'check: Document submittal records and Austin Energy coordination correspondence.' While the Master Comment Report clearly evidences Austin Energy coordination (dedicated reviewer, active Bluebeam comment link), the actual document submission cannot be verified from the available materials.

perRunFindings.comment: Title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey with certification showing all easement encumbrances not submitted to Austin Energy for review. Applicant must obtain and submit to Austin Energy a formal title document (title commitment, title policy, ALTA/ACSM survey, or Ownership/Encumbrance Report) certified to show all existing easements and encumbrances affecting the property.
applicableAreas: All proposed and modified electric easement areas
perRunFindings.observation: No title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey certified to show all existing easement encumbrances is evident in the supplementary documents reviewed. The facts.md document identifies six existing easements of record (greenbelt access, drainage, wastewater, drainage, public utility, drainage) but does not indicate submission of a title document showing all encumbrances.
